title: Filtration of a constructible sheaf by extensions by zero of lisse sheaves
statement:
Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme, $\Lambda=E$ or $\Qlb$, and $F\in\Cons(X,\Lambda)$. Let
$S_1,\dots,S_m$ be a stratification adapted to $F$, ordered as in
[det-lem-coefficient-heart-common-stratification] (1), so that $V_k=S_1\cup\dots\cup S_k$ is
open, with open immersions $v_k\colon V_k\hookrightarrow X$, and let $a_k\colon S_k\hookrightarrow X$.
Put $F_k=v_{k!}v_k^*F\subseteq F$. Then
$$
0=F_0\subseteq F_1\subseteq\dots\subseteq F_m=F,\qquad F_k/F_{k-1}\cong a_{k!}(F|_{S_k}),
$$
and each $F|_{S_k}$ is lisse.
Here $V_0=\varnothing$, and lisse means locally free of finite rank for the pro-étale topology. The category $\Cons(X,\Lambda)$ is the category of constructible $\Lambda_X$-modules of [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. For a locally closed immersion $a\colon S\hookrightarrow X$, write $a=i\circ u$, where $u\colon S\hookrightarrow\overline S$ is open and $i\colon\overline S\hookrightarrow X$ is closed, and define $a_!=i_*u_!$. The inclusions in the filtration need not be strict.

proof.text:
By [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients] (1), for every scheme morphism $h:T\to W$ used below the canonical coefficient map $h^{-1}\Lambda_W\to\Lambda_T$ is an isomorphism. Thus the inverse-image coefficient rings in the localization and base-change statements are the specified $\Lambda_T$, and module pullback is the exact inverse-image functor; all subsequent functor identifications use these canonical coefficient isomorphisms. Every open subscheme of $X$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian], hence quasi-compact, and is quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated]. Every open immersion into such a scheme is quasi-compact: its inverse image over an affine open is an open subscheme of a Noetherian scheme, hence quasi-compact by the former node. Thus [det-sf-open-closed-sequence-ring-sheaf] applies with $B=\Lambda_X$, and also on each $V_k$, with the restricted coefficient ring. Its clause (3) makes the counit $F_k=v_{k!}v_k^*F\to F$ a monomorphism. For $w\colon V_{k-1}\hookrightarrow V_k$, clause (1) gives, naturally in $N$ and $M$,
$$\operatorname{Hom}(v_{k!}w_!N,M)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(N,w^*v_k^*M)=\operatorname{Hom}(N,v_{k-1}^*M)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(v_{k-1!}N,M).$$
The corresponding canonical isomorphism $v_{k!}w_!\simeq v_{k-1!}$ identifies the composite $v_{k!}w_!w^*v_k^*F\to v_{k!}v_k^*F\to F$ with the counit for $v_{k-1}$: both correspond to the identity of $v_{k-1}^*F$ under these adjunction bijections. This gives the inclusion $F_{k-1}\subseteq F_k$ over $F$. Extension from the empty open is zero (it is the left adjoint from the zero module category), and extension along the identity is the identity, so $F_0=0$ and $F_m=F$.

source.place: First paragraph: counit subobjects, nested opens and endpoints.

proof.text:
Fix $1\leq k\leq m$. Put $G=v_k^*F$, let $w\colon V_{k-1}\hookrightarrow V_k$, and let $c\colon S_k\hookrightarrow V_k$ be its closed complement. By [det-sf-open-closed-sequence-ring-sheaf] (3),
$$0\to w_!w^*G\to G\to c_*c^*G\to0$$
is exact. All quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness hypotheses were checked in step 1. Apply the exact functor $v_{k!}$ from clause (1), and use the canonical composition and counit identification proved in step 1. Since $c^*G=F|_{S_k}$, this gives
$$0\to F_{k-1}\to F_k\to v_{k!}c_*(F|_{S_k})\to0.$$
The first map is the inclusion over $F$ constructed in step 1, so its cokernel is the stated subsheaf quotient $F_k/F_{k-1}$.

source.place: Second paragraph: the localization sequence on V_k and exact v_k!.

proof.text:
We identify the last term with $a_{k!}(F|_{S_k})$ by an actual canonical isomorphism. Write $Y=\overline{S_k}$, $i\colon Y\hookrightarrow X$, $u\colon S_k\hookrightarrow Y$, and $q\colon X\setminus Y\hookrightarrow X$. Since $S_k$ is closed in $V_k$, the square with sides $c,v_k,u,i$ is Cartesian: $Y\times_XV_k=S_k$. The closed scheme $Y$ is Noetherian: a finite affine cover of $X$ restricts to closed affines with coordinate rings $A/I$, whose ideals lift to ideals of the Noetherian ring $A$; its underlying closed subspace is quasi-compact. It is quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated]. All open subschemes needed below are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian], and their open inclusions are quasi-compact as in step 1.
For a $\Lambda_{S_k}$-module $N$, put $H=v_{k!}c_*N$. Clause (4) of [det-sf-open-closed-sequence-ring-sheaf], applied to the Cartesian square above, and clause (2) on $V_k$ give
$$i^*H\simeq u_!c^*c_*N\simeq u_!N.$$
The same open base-change formula along $q$ expresses $q^*H$ as extension from $V_k\setminus Y$ of the restriction of $c_*N$. That restriction is zero by clause (2), because $V_k\setminus Y$ is disjoint from $S_k$. Therefore $q^*H=0$. Clause (3) for the pair $(q,i)$ now makes the unit $H\to i_*i^*H$ an isomorphism. Composing gives
$$v_{k!}c_*N\simeq i_*u_!N=a_{k!}N.$$
Substitute $N=F|_{S_k}$ in step 2 to obtain $F_k/F_{k-1}\simeq a_{k!}(F|_{S_k})$. Finally the stratification is adapted to $F$, so [det-lem-coefficient-heart-closure], in its constructible/lisse characterization, says each $F|_{S_k}$ is lisse. If the filtration is regarded inside $\Cons(X,\Lambda)$, its terms lie there as well: open base change in clause (4) restricts $F_k$ to $F$ on the earlier strata and to zero on the later ones. For the latter assertion, clause (3) applied to $v_{k!}N$ has its first arrow an isomorphism by clause (1) and the triangle identity; hence the restriction to the closed complement is zero by clause (2). The same adapted stratification therefore verifies constructibility by the cited characterization.

tool_uses.why: Generic open–closed localization for module sheaves over an arbitrary sheaf of rings supplies exactness, adjunction, and the short exact sequence; the coefficient-heart route has no separate node proving this ambient sheaf theorem.
Generic Noetherian-open result verifies that each V_k is quasi-compact, a hypothesis of the localization tool.
Generic locally-Noetherian quasi-separatedness verifies the remaining qcqs hypothesis of the localization tool.

The Cartesian coefficient isomorphism identifies inverse-image coefficient rings with the prescribed E or Qlb coefficient sheaves, so the generic ring-sheaf localization tool applies in the stated module categories.
